allocation_tooling: No allocator counters on this host (same classification as Plan 240). Evidence is mechanical source accounting, not measured counts.

F1_always_chunked_tower_responses.detail: response_from_http_body takes the streaming path whenever !body.is_end_stream() at construction, which is true even for fully-buffered Full bodies with exact size hints. Every Tower/Axum response is therefore unknown-length chunked; Content-Length is never emitted. Wire proof: tower 1 KiB GET returns transfer-encoding: chunked where native returns content-length: 1024.
F1_always_chunked_tower_responses.evidence: DEBUG head capture during matrix development (tower resp0 head: date + transfer-encoding: chunked, no content-length); interop.rs response_from_http_body fast-path condition
F1_always_chunked_tower_responses.impact: Extra chunk framing bytes per response; clients cannot preallocate; HTTP/1.0 downgrade/clients requiring length suffer. Throughput impact below noise for 1 MiB (bytes dominate).
F1_always_chunked_tower_responses.recommendation_295: PROCEED as optimization candidate P1: honor exact size_hint (known-length fast path) while keeping framing authority runtime-owned. Stop if size_hint cannot be trusted without polling.

F2_stream_policy_unconsumed_body_forces_.detail: With RequestBodyPolicy::Stream, a Tower service that never polls the request body triggers connection: close even on a bodyless GET. The default TowerToEggserve::new() (Stream 1 MiB) + Axum GET shape therefore cannot reuse keep-alive connections: every response closes. Reject policy on the same bodyless GET keeps alive.
F2_stream_policy_unconsumed_body_forces_.evidence: matrix development: tower+Stream resp0 head contained connection: close + chunked; tower+Reject head had no connection: close and sustained 500 sequential keep-alive requests. Pinned by CI test baseline_294_stream_policy_unconsumed_body_connection_behavior.
F2_stream_policy_unconsumed_body_forces_.impact: For downstream servers using the default constructor, connection churn replaces keep-alive reuse on every request: new TCP handshake + slow-start per request. This dwarfs the ~13us adaptation cost.
F2_stream_policy_unconsumed_body_forces_.recommendation_295: PROCEED as optimization candidate P2 with strict framing-safety stop conditions: complete-but-unpolled bodies (zero declared bytes, nothing on the wire) must not force close; any case with unread wire bytes keeps the current close. If the lifecycle state machine cannot distinguish these without redesign, DEFER to a corrective plan instead of weakening framing safety.

F3_h1_response_trailers_never_reach_wire.detail: Hyper's H1 server encodes response trailers only when the response head declares them via a Trailer header (hyper 1.11.1 role.rs: into_chunked_with_trailing_fields). EggServe strips Trailer as runtime-owned hop-by-hop and never synthesizes it, so H1 response trailers are silently dropped for native AND tower paths alike, even with TE: trailers and a valid terminal block. Adapter-level proof: to_hyper_response emits the trailers frame; normalization preserves it (has_response_trailers=true); the wire shows 0-chunk with no trailer section.
F3_h1_response_trailers_never_reach_wire.evidence: ka_probe wire captures; hyper 1.11.1 encode.rs Chunked(None) => None ('trailer header is not set'); parity test baseline_294_terminal_trailer_parity pins native/tower convergence
F3_h1_response_trailers_never_reach_wire.impact: Any consumer relying on H1 response trailers gets silent data loss of the trailer section (body intact).
F3_h1_response_trailers_never_reach_wire.recommendation_295: NO-GO for 295/296. Requires a separate scoped correctness plan (head-time Trailer declaration needs trailer-field lookahead the current one-shot future shape cannot provide without buffering). Recorded as unresolved finding; convergence test prevents silent divergence.
